context:
Reuse existing DataFrameMaintenanceOperations protocol (maintenance_interface.py:300-427)
and get_maintenance_operations_for_platform() (maintenance_interface.py:783-866) as the
DataFrame backend's write layer. Follow the WritePrimitivesBenchmark pattern
(write_primitives/benchmark.py:1196-1287) for capability-driven DataFrame execution.

Extract SQL logic from benchmark.py into SQLETLBackend - this is a move, not a rewrite.
The _load_warehouse_data(), validate_etl_results(), and SCD processor SQL methods become
methods on SQLETLBackend. The existing run_etl_pipeline() becomes the shared orchestrator
that accepts a backend parameter instead of a connection.

Phase order matters: backend protocol first, then Transform refactor, then wiring, then
cleanup. Run tests after each phase.
description:
TPC-DI's execute_dataframe_workload() currently resolves a SQL connection via
SQLConnectionProvider.get_sql_connection() and passes it to run_etl_pipeline(),
which executes raw SQL INSERT INTO, executemany(), executescript(), and validation
via SELECT COUNT(*). The DataFrame variant should NEVER use SQL.

The fix: introduce a TPCDIETLBackend protocol with SQL and DataFrame implementations.
Extract a shared mode-agnostic ETL orchestrator for Extract + Transform, then create
separate Load/Validate/SCD backends. The DataFrame backend delegates to the existing
DataFrameMaintenanceOperations protocol (insert_rows, update_rows, merge_rows).
Additionally, eliminate the double CSV serialization in the Transform phase by having
transforms return DataFrames directly.

SQLConnectionProvider and get_sql_connection() are removed entirely from the
DataFrame subsystem since the concept is architecturally wrong - DataFrame adapters
should never be asked for SQL connections.

anti_patterns.why: DataFrameMaintenanceOperations already provides insert_rows/update_rows/merge_rows with per-platform implementations

anti_patterns.dont: keep staging CSV files as an intermediate format
anti_patterns.why: the Transform phase already produces pandas DataFrames internally and writing/reading CSVs is wasteful double I/O
the DataFrame subsystem should never expose SQL concepts

anti_patterns.instead: only extract their logic into SQLETLBackend
anti_patterns.why: run_etl_benchmark and run_full_benchmark must continue working identically

preserves.behavior: DataFrameMaintenanceOperations protocol and its concrete implementations (Polars, Delta Lake, Iceberg, DuckLake) are not modified
ETLPhaseResult, ETLBatchResult, ETLResult dataclasses in etl/results.py are not modified
Existing DataFrame platform tests (test_benchmark_mixin.py) continue to pass
SQL path (run_etl_benchmark → run_etl_pipeline → SQL INSERT) continues to work exactly as before via SQLETLBackend
TPC-DI stage result schema (query_id, status, execution_time, records_processed, records_loaded, rows_returned, first_row) is unchanged
run_full_benchmark() and all SQL-mode TPC-DI entry points remain unbroken
